title: Lesson 11: Managing a Client Portfolio Strategically
description: How a principal allocates scarce delivery capability across accounts already held, deciding which to expand, which to renew, and which to let churn on purpose.

questions.question: Why is the unit of analysis for portfolio management the account rather than a single engagement?
options: Because accounts are billed monthly while engagements are billed on milestones.
Because the levers cross engagement boundaries, so the relationship needs an owner accountable beyond the work in flight.
Because clients insist on one point of contact for commercial questions.
Because engagement-level data is not available in the delivery system.
questions.explanation: The expansion, renewal, and churn levers act on the whole relationship, so the unit of analysis is the account rather than one engagement.

questions.question: What is the strategic test for whether an expansion genuinely improves the portfolio?
options: Reuse: whether the next engagement can lean on captured skills and method, so marginal cost falls.
Whether the account will pay a higher rate for the second engagement than the first.
Whether the expansion keeps the delivery team at full utilization.
Whether the expansion is larger in revenue than the engagement it follows.
questions.explanation: An expansion compounds only when it reuses existing capability, lowering marginal cost instead of pulling the team into a new domain.

questions.question: An account buys the lowest-margin work and drains senior capability from the practice. How should a principal treat it?
options: Renew it but staff it with junior operators to protect the margin.
Keep it, since all revenue is good and churn is always the enemy.
Convert it to an hourly model so the attention cost becomes visible.
Treat it as a candidate for intentional churn, freeing capability for accounts that compound.
questions.explanation: An account that consumes more capability than it returns is worth winding down deliberately, so the freed capability can fund accounts that compound.
